title: Launch plan + internal enablement for Quickstart Templates (RAG + agents)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
sub_issues: PM-915-1: Finalize launch gates + go/no-go checklist
PM-915-2: Comms + docs publish checklist (internal + external)
PM-915-3: Support enablement (runbooks + macros + escalation path)
PM-915-5: Post-launch cadence + KPI dashboard review ritual
body:
Context
- DevEx is building “Quickstart templates” for RAG + agents that are production-minded by default (safe defaults, streaming robustness, cost controls, guardrails) with standardized observability (OTel + Redwood conventions).
- This ticket defines how we launch (internal beta → public), how we message it, and how we enable Support + Sales Engineering to handle early volume without creating noise or regressions.

Goals
- Make templates discoverable and trustworthy for self-serve developers while being supportable for enterprise evaluations.
- Ensure we have a clear go/no-go bar (security, reliability, observability, docs) and a plan for rapid iteration after launch.
- Ensure adoption telemetry is privacy-safe and operationally safe (no breaking proxies by default headers).

Non-goals
- Not a product marketing launch (no major press). This is a docs-first + DevEx launch with light announcement.
- Not committing to long-term support for every framework/tooling combination; scope is Python + TypeScript v1 only.

Launch scope (v1)
- Templates
  - Python: RAG + agent baseline (tool calling, retriever abstraction, eval hooks, Docker + local OTel collector).
  - TypeScript: RAG + agent baseline (streaming, retries defaults, instrumentation, structured output / tool schema validation patterns).
- Template CLI
  - Commands: init, doctor.
  - Version stamp written at scaffold time.
- Observability pack integration
  - Prebuilt dashboards (RAG latency breakdown, tool failure rate, retrieval hit rate, token economics).
  - Recommended alerts/SLO examples (documented as “optional, tune to your traffic”).
- Docs
  - Docs IA includes “Quickstart Templates” section; walkthrough for RAG+agents; troubleshooting; observability hooks reference.

Launch stages + target dates (proposed)
1) Internal beta (DONE)
   - Target: DevEx, SRE, Support, Solutions Engineering, a few friendly customers.
   - Goal: flush out install issues, OTel collector misconfig, streaming disconnects, tool schema parse errors.
2) Public docs + repo availability (TARGET: 2025-03-25)
   - Templates repo public + docs site published + CLI install instructions.
   - Announce in community channels (Docs “What’s new”, small blog note if time).
3) Harden + iterate (Weeks 1–4 post-launch)
   - Weekly patch releases (templates) as needed; SDK patch releases only if required.
   - Tight feedback loop with Support + #help triage.

Go/No-Go gates (must be true to ship)
- Security / privacy
  - No secrets in logs by default; redaction processors enabled in sample collector config.
  - Telemetry tags are opt-in (no default extra headers that could be blocked by corporate proxies).
  - Dependencies pinned + vuln scanning enabled; Renovate (or equivalent) configured for safe updates.
- Reliability / streaming
  - Default timeouts and retry/backoff match “safe defaults” policy; streaming reconnect behavior documented.
  - CI smoke tests pass (streaming + tool calling + basic retrieval correctness) with flake mitigation documented.
- Observability
  - Request IDs propagate into logs and traces.
  - Spans emitted with agreed naming + attributes; metric dimensions reviewed for cardinality risks.
  - Dashboards render with sample data using local dev recipe.
- Docs quality
  - Standard README structure across templates (setup, run, deploy options, troubleshooting, verifying observability, cost controls).
  - Troubleshooting covers top issues: 401/invalid key, 429 rate limits, timeouts, tool schema validation errors, retrieval returns empty.

Comms checklist
Internal
- Post internal “launch ready” note to #announcements + #devex + #support-internal
  - What shipped, what changed since beta, known limitations, how to give feedback.
  - Escalation path + oncall owner for first 2 weeks.
- Send enablement email to Support + Solutions Engineering
  - Links: template repo, docs walkthrough, troubleshooting, observability hooks reference, demo script.
External (lightweight)
- Docs “What’s new” entry
- Community post (Discord/Slack community) pointing to templates section + CLI
- Optional: short blog post (if bandwidth) focused on “production-minded defaults” and “observability out of the box” (no benchmark claims).

Internal enablement
Support (Owner: Dev Patel; Support feedback loop: Priya Shah)
- Create support playbook:
  - Triage decision tree: auth → quota/429 → networking/streaming → tool schema → retrieval config → OTel exporter.
  - Required artifacts to request from user: template version stamp, runtime logs (redacted), request ID, collector logs, proxy details if streaming issues.
  - Known issues + mitigations:
    - Corporate proxies blocking unknown headers: ensure telemetry tagging disabled unless user opts in; document how to remove/disable.
    - OTel exporter auth failing: verify endpoint + headers; provide minimal working env example.
    - 429s during quickstart: recommend lower concurrency + exponential backoff; clarify default QPS expectations.
- Draft 6 macros for top issues (for Zendesk/Jira responses), including “how to verify observability is working”.
- Escalation path for the first 14 days post-launch:
  - P0: widespread template breakage / docs wrong causing data loss or security risk → DevEx oncall + SRE reviewer.
  - P1: streaming disconnect patterns behind proxies → SDK leads + DevEx.

Sales Engineering / Solutions (Owner: Renee Sullivan + Solutions Eng partner)
- Demo script:
  - 5–7 minute “from zero to running”: init → configure env → run → show dashboard + traces → show troubleshooting view.
  - “Enterprise angle”: Dedicated vs Private deployment notes; redaction guidance; audit-friendly logs.
- FAQ sheet (1 pager):
  - “What is supported in v1?” “How do updates work?” “Can I swap models/providers?” “What telemetry is collected?”

Docs enablement (Owner: Elliot Price; Writer: Wei Chen)
- Ensure docs are cross-linked from SDK guides and from RAG documentation.
- Add “Latest vs pinned” guidance consistent with template release process:
  - Recommend pinning template version for production; provide upgrade notes and changelog link.

Telemetry + KPIs (Owner: Logan Wright; PM: Nikhil/Henry)
- Success metrics to monitor weekly (first 4 weeks)
  - Activation: time-to-first-success (TTFS) funnel from “template init” → “first successful API call” → “first trace emitted”.
  - Template retention: % of users still active after 7/14 days (tagged traffic).
  - Support deflection: drop in “how do I set up streaming/OTel/retries” tickets; track macro usage.
  - Quality: error rates by category (auth/quota/network/tool/retrieval), streaming disconnect rate, tool schema validation failure rate.
- Privacy constraints
  - No PII in telemetry; no prompts/responses in metrics; logs are redacted by default.
  - Telemetry tags/header must be optional and documented.

Post-launch iteration cadence
- Week 0–2
  - Daily triage (15 min) in DevEx + Support channel; tag issues with severity and whether docs-only vs code change.
  - Patch releases as needed (templates) with strict changelog discipline.
- Week 3–4
  - Move to weekly triage; cluster feedback into: onboarding friction, reliability, observability, deployment recipes, SDK gaps.
- Monthly
  - Template roadmap review: new templates vs hardening vs deprecations.

Risks / open questions
- Risk: telemetry tagging breaks corporate proxies if we ship default headers.
  - Mitigation: keep telemetry opt-in; provide query-param or config-based tagging alternative if needed.
- Risk: high-cardinality attributes accidentally shipped in spans/metrics.
  - Mitigation: Observability review required; run a “cardinality checklist” in PR review.
- Open question: how we present provider abstraction in docs without implying full compatibility guarantees.
  - Proposed: “Redwood-first, provider-agnostic patterns; adapters are examples; validate in your environment.”

References (existing artifacts)
- Confluence: Quickstart Templates project brief; template requirements; observability hooks standard; safe defaults and guardrails; release process; docs IA update.
- Linear: PM-912 (telemetry requirements), PM-913 (supported models), PM-914 (safe defaults), ENG-4182..4187 (implementation), DES-377/378 (README + diagram).

Recent updates
- 2025-03-18 (Henry): Added proxy-header risk as explicit go/no-go item; aligning with DevEx on making template telemetry tagging opt-in only.
- 2025-03-14 (Nikhil): Support enablement scope expanded to include OTel exporter auth failure macro (seen in beta). Need confirmation from Observability on the minimal collector config we should recommend.

Next actions
- Henry (PM) + Monica (DevEx): confirm final ship date and publish checklist owners.
- Dev Patel/Priya: deliver support macros + escalation plan by 2025-03-21.
- Elliot/Wei: ensure docs cross-links + troubleshooting are complete by 2025-03-22.
- Allison/Sergio: confirm dashboards + alert rules are published/linked and do not assume non-default exporters by 2025-03-22.
- Logan: confirm KPI dashboard definitions + filters for template-tagged traffic by 2025-03-24.
